kept.heading: "GAMERS DON'T HATE ADS; THEY HATE BAD ADS" – WHY EA AND XBOX ARE PUTTING ADVERTS IN THEIR GAMES (7 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: In-game advertising offers publishers a growing revenue stream, but player experience determines its success. EA plans to sell ads integrated into game environments, while Xbox is testing ads before streaming sessions in exchange for free access. Mobile in-game ads generated $28B in 2025, but console and PC players are more resistant. Research shows 1 in 5 players would play more with high-quality ads, while 1 in 5 have quit due to poor ad experiences.

kept.heading: AI SEARCH META ANALYSIS - Q4 2026 (11 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: AI Overviews are appearing on more commercial searches, with one study finding coverage across 88% of its sampled keywords. Their presence can reduce organic clicks by up to 40%. AI platforms are also influencing brand discovery and product shortlists, though visibility doesn't always translate into website visits or purchases. Consumers remain less comfortable letting AI agents complete purchases.

kept.heading: HOW TO NOT DO PR (10 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: PR campaigns need a newsworthy headline backed by substantial data. Focus each article on one story and use clear charts to visualize findings. Add your own commentary and secure expert quotes to strengthen credibility and encourage sharing. Include methodology and contact details to build trust. For outreach, find relevant journalists through recent Google News coverage. Start with niche publications and pitch on Tuesday, then follow up on Friday.

kept.heading: LINKEDIN SAYS INFLUENTIAL VOICES ARE CRITICAL FOR AI CHATBOT CITATIONS (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Accounts with over 10K followers and company pages make up 65% of LinkedIn citations in AI chatbot responses. Executive and VP-level articles also earn more citations per article. LinkedIn recommends building authority through consistent employee posts across 3-4 themes and partnerships with 1-2 relevant creators.

kept.heading: MCP FOR MARKETERS: WHAT MODEL CONTEXT PROTOCOL MEANS FOR MEDIA AND MEASUREMENT (10 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Google, Amazon, and TikTok now offer MCP integrations that let AI applications retrieve advertising data and manage campaigns. This overview explains how MCP works and compares what each platform's integrations allow agents to do. It examines how inconsistent attribution creates gaps in cross-channel measurement and how independent data can improve budget decisions. It also covers 6 stages of agent adoption, from answering performance questions to executing campaign changes with defined permissions and human oversight.

kept.heading: HOW DO YOU ADVERTISE AI TO AN INCREASINGLY SKEPTICAL PUBLIC? (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Consumer ads are moving away from the term “AI” as it risks alienating skeptical audiences. Instead, campaigns focus on product benefits without mentioning the technology. Messaging works best when it stays neutral and avoids framing AI as either revolutionary or something to apologize for.

kept.heading: PERMISSION IS A USEFUL MARKETING SIGNAL (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: An informational newsletter offers a simple way to gauge whether content is resonating. When someone subscribes, they give permission for ongoing communication, signaling that your content has earned their interest. Tracking sign-ups helps identify where potential customers are engaging or losing interest without relying on complex attribution tools. Newsletters can also fuel social posts and resource offers that encourage more subscriptions.

kept.heading: I GOT A 2M-FOLLOWER LINKEDIN PAGE TO POST OUR MEMES (FOR FREE) (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Create branded memes about audience pain points and email them to large niche LinkedIn pages for free reposts.

kept.heading: RETAILERS ARE TURNING TO ENTERTAINMENT TO WIN SHOPPERS' ATTENTION (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Retailers investing in experiential stores saw average basket size rise close to 10% YoY.

kept.heading: HOLIDAY ADS ARE STARTING EARLIER. SHOPPERS MAY NOT BE. (1 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Retailers are increasing holiday ad spending earlier in the year, but consumers are not necessarily starting their shopping earlier. Nielsen found six times more holiday advertising in September than five years ago, while historical data shows that holiday ads on connected TV can generate up to 3.2 times the sales lift of non-holiday ads. The earlier push gives brands more time to build awareness and consideration, but it also risks ad fatigue before shoppers are ready to buy. An earlier advertising schedule does not mean an earlier customer journey, so brands need to build interest before introducing timely offers that give consumers a reason to purchase.

kept.heading: WHY SOME SHOPPERS SKIP COUPONS—EVEN WHEN THEY OFFER A DEAL (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Consumers who believe businesses use discounts for self-serving reasons are less likely to redeem coupons. Research found that shoppers with higher power distance beliefs often question whether a coupon represents genuine savings or signals inflated prices or product problems. You can improve coupon redemption by clearly explaining the offer, addressing skepticism about pricing, and offering price-matching guarantees. The research also found that coupon campaigns may perform better in regions with lower power distance beliefs, making cultural attitudes a useful factor in audience targeting.

kept.heading: JUST ADMIT “I DON'T KNOW” (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Admitting when you don't know an answer can increase customer trust and purchase intent more than giving a vague response. A study found that vague answers made customers up to 16% less likely to buy than answers that acknowledged uncertainty and promised to find the information. This effect was strongest when customers suspected salespeople had a personal financial incentive, such as earning commission. Explain how you'll get the answer rather than leaving customers with uncertainty, since a clear and honest response makes you seem more trustworthy and collaborative.

kept.heading: EXPLORE PITCH
YOU CAN NOW ADD AMAZON AFFILIATE LINKS TO YOUR INSTAGRAM REELS (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Instagram is expanding its shopping features by letting eligible US creators add Amazon affiliate links directly to Reels and feed posts. Creators earn commissions on qualifying purchases without Instagram taking a cut. Product links also work in carousels and support affiliate platforms like LTK and ShopMy. Creators can now turn entire product collections and gift guides into shoppable content using a single link.

kept.heading: HOW GOOGLE REDIRECT URLS CAN DISTORT A RANK-TRACKING EXPORT (5 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Google rank-tracking tools can record a result's position without identifying the actual page it links to when Google redirect URLs are not properly identified. In one November 2026 snapshot, 63 of 65 organic results contained these redirects, making URL comparisons unreliable because different redirect links can lead to the same page. Check where each link leads before analyzing keyword overlap, page rankings, or site visibility. Keep the original URLs, provider, and collection date so your SEO reporting remains accurate and easy to verify.

kept.heading: HOW (& HOW NOT) TO USE AI FOR KEYWORD RESEARCH (17 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: AI is most useful for keyword research when it analyzes data a business already has rather than generating keyword lists from scratch. Customer emails and call notes can be turned into search phrases, with the customer's original wording kept separate from AI suggestions. A short brief listing services, location, and what the business doesn't offer stops the model from suggesting irrelevant keywords. Search Console exports and PPC search terms reports can then be sorted into page assignments and negative keyword candidates, with every figure checked in the source platform.

kept.heading: HOW I BROKE THROUGH MY AI PLATEAU (5 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: After hitting an AI plateau, the author found new momentum by building a personal app to surface overlooked photography and creating a shared “marketing brain” in GitHub with Claude. The experience reinforced the value of solving personal problems with AI and exchanging practical learnings with peers. Rather than treating AI as a fixed set of workflows, the approach is to keep experimenting while protecting skills, like writing and critical thinking, that are worth developing independently.

kept.heading: WHAT WE LEARNED BY WATCHING CLAUDE READ ZAPIER.COM (5 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Zapier built an experimental tool to test how Claude interprets website content. When testing its Slack integration page, the team discovered that Claude wasn't reading the modified webpage directly. Instead, it retrieved a Markdown version and passed the content through another AI model before the main model processed it. This means changes to a webpage's HTML may not affect what AI agents actually see. Testing how AI reads Markdown content is just as important.

kept.heading: AMAZON SPONSORED BRANDS, PRICED BY WHERE THEY SHOW (11 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: A guide to Amazon Sponsored Brands formats, placement performance, bidding strategies, costs, and 2026 updates.

kept.heading: MARKETERS TO SPEND $116 BILLION ON CREATORS IN 2026 (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Brand spending on creators is forecast to grow 15% in 2026 and reach $178 billion by 2030, about twice the pace of advertising. Paid amplification of creator content makes up 44% of spending, while paying creators for content rather than reach is the fastest-growing segment. Most of the growth comes from budgets shifted out of TV, performance media, and creative production rather than new marketing dollars.

kept.heading: 94% OF GLOBAL HITS WENT VIRAL ON TIKTOK FIRST, REVEALS 2026 MUSIC IMPACT REPORT (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: TikTok has become a major driver of music discovery and commercial success. 94% of songs that entered the Billboard Global 200 in 2025 went viral on the platform first. Songs that go viral on TikTok spend four times longer on the chart than non-viral tracks, and 45% of US TikTok users discover new music on the platform. That discovery also translates into purchases: TikTok music listeners are 78% more likely to pay for a streaming subscription, and 61% purchased physical or digital music in the past year.

kept.heading: WIN REPORT: HOW CUTTING OVERWHELM GREW CONVERSIONS BY 13% (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Reducing the effort required to compare options can increase conversions, especially when a page overwhelms visitors with too much information. Churnet Valley Railway replaced its long list of eight dining experiences with categorized sections that put popular options first and compact cards that made prices, departure times, and durations easy to compare. It also replaced the “Book Now” CTA with “Check Running Times” to give visitors a lower-commitment next step into the booking process. The redesign increased conversions by 13%, with an even stronger result among first-time visitors.

kept.heading: 5 WAYS TO PERSONALIZE YOUR EMAILS, FROM A STUDY OF 274 BILLION SENDS (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Personalize emails by referencing shoppers' recent activity, such as products they browsed, items in their cart, or their last purchase. Use signup preferences to tailor welcome emails, and include product-specific care tips, how-to content, or complementary product recommendations in post-purchase emails. Show/hide logic can also display different content to different segments in a single campaign, such as VIP offers for loyalty members or location-specific promotions. Klaviyo's analysis of 274 billion emails found that messages that referenced shoppers' recent activity earned 45% higher click rates in flows and 33% higher click rates in campaigns.

kept.heading: WRITESTACK (TOOL)
kept.blurb: WriteStack is a Substack growth platform that helps creators turn Notes into free and paid subscribers. Its AI Coach generates Notes and outlines in the creator's voice and helps edit articles. Creators can batch schedule Notes and use analytics to see which posts drive subscriptions. The platform also streamlines notifications and supports cross-posting to other social channels, and AI agent integrations.

kept.heading: THE AI AD CREATIVE MASTERCLASS: SKILLS, TOOLS, AND THE 21 FORMATS TOP BRANDS RUN (15 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: 24 of the 34 longest-running Meta ads from 48 top DTC brands were simple stills. Creator videos were the most tested video format but among the first switched off, with a median run of 38 days. Strong batches mix at least 4 formats and 3 buying angles, with stills built to run for months and videos replaced every few weeks.

kept.heading: WHY YOU WANT MORE UNSUBSCRIBES (8 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: A very low unsubscribe rate can mean email is landing in spam, since nobody unsubscribes from a junk folder. Unsubscribing is also the least damaging way to leave, since a spam report hurts placement and silent non-readers drag it down over time. Splitting unsubscribes by opt-in type separates intentional sign-ups, whose exits signal a content problem, from consequential ones like gated downloads, whose quick exits are expected. Making the exit easy, and occasionally inviting it, keeps people who are done from reaching for the spam button.

kept.heading: AI PRODUCT RECOMMENDATIONS ARE MOSTLY A SUMMARY OF LISTICLES (7 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: A study across 4 search engines found that 90% of recommended brands appeared on at least one cited “best X” or “top X” list. Brands featured on 3 or more cited lists were recommended 44% of the time, compared with just 2.5% for brands absent from all lists. The top 10 list publishers accounted for up to 90% of citations in some categories. Updated comparisons also mattered, with 83% of Gemini's cited pages featuring 2026 in the title or URL.

kept.heading: 3 THINGS I'M WATCHING IN MARKETING GOING INTO 2027 (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Brands are replacing some agency work with in-house creators and employee advocates to build trust through individual voices. Engaged communities are becoming more valuable than large follower counts as brands seek direct audience relationships beyond algorithm-dependent platforms. Meanwhile, audiences are tuning out generic claims of authenticity. Original perspectives and behind-the-scenes content are becoming more effective ways to stand out.

kept.heading: WHEN DID ‘GRAND THEFT AUTO' BECOME BRAND SAFE? (10 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: GTA is no longer an automatic brand safety risk, but brands must weigh its cultural relevance against whether its provocative world fits their identity and audience.

kept.heading: GOOGLE IS MAKING MORE ROOM FOR NEWS IN AI SEARCH (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Sites like Reddit report receiving less traffic from Google despite frequent appearances in AI answers.
